chunks: And a group of scholars informed us, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh, who said: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Matil informed us, saying:

There was a woman called Zainab from the people of Aba. She was the wife of Muhammad ibn Abdillah al-Abi, and she had three hundred dinars with her. She went to my uncle Ja'far ibn Ahmad ibn Matil and said: 'I wish for this money to be transferred from my hand to the hand of Abu al-Qasim ibn Ruh (may Allah be pleased with him).' He said: 'Let me go with her to translate for her.' When she entered upon Abu al-Qasim ibn Ruh (may Allah be pleased with him), he addressed her in the eloquent tongue of his father, the Master of Vision (Sahib al-Basir), and said to her: 'Zainab, kun-tu kun-tu bada kuliya junis-tu.' Its meaning is: 'How are you and how were you, and what is the news of your children?' She did not need my translation, handed over the money, and returned.

key_terms.أَبُو الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ رُوحٍ: Abu al-Qasim ibn Ruh, the Second Imam's deputy (deputy of the deputy)
key_terms.دِينَارٍ: Dinar, a gold coin used as currency
key_terms.صَاحِبَ الْبَصِيرِ: Sahib al-Basir, a title for Ubayd Allah ibn Abi al-Khattab, father of the Second Imam's deputy

ai.seo_question: How did the Second Imam's father communicate with Zainab to facilitate the transfer of her wealth?
ai.summary: This narrative from *Kitab al-Ghayba* illustrates the unique status of Abu al-Qasim ibn Ruh as the 'Major Deputy' (al-Na'ib al-Akbar) of the Twelfth Imam, demonstrating his authority to receive and manage the financial trusts (khums and gifts) of the faithful. The detail of the Imam speaking in a familiar dialect, rendering translation unnecessary, underscores the accessibility and personal connection between the Imam and his community during the Minor Exile, reinforcing the legitimacy of his role as the intermediary between the Hidden Imam and the believers.
